Limitations: PGS001280 is from a known pan-trait UKB framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as often less externally robust than disease-focused scores; additionally, the endpoint is time-to-event (a mild negative signal for generic disease-risk use). Competing PE-specific models either have weaker endpoint specificity (PE±DVT composites) or lack PRS-only metrics (PGS004460/PGS004530), and the EAS-only model (PGS003861) reports only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates, making it non-comparable as standalone PRS evidence.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target concept (pulmonary fibrosis), with two specifically aligned to idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). PGS001791 is preferred because it has strong endpoint fidelity (trait/phenotyping both IPF), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant coverage (910,439), and comes from a multi-biobank/global analysis context with European evaluation; it also reports a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.005929), which is interpretable without relying on full-model AUROC. The main limitation is that the evidence remains mixed/insufficient for a clearly high-quality pick: PGS001791’s PRS signal is modest and lacks a reported PGS-only AUROC, while PGS001030 reports an explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.6252) and PGS-only R2 (0.0142) but is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (a known weaker archetype) and its very high full-model AUROC appears largely covariate-driven (incremental AUROC 0.01818). PGS004695 has good IPF alignment and a strong HR (3.78 high vs low quintile) but lacks standard PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and uses a small GWAS-hits SNP set (23), making cross-model comparability and standalone PRS strength harder to judge.

All four candidates are direct matches to retinal detachment by trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, but they come from UK Biobank framework/portability papers rather than a disease-focused multi-cohort retinal detachment study, which domain guidance flags as a common source of weaker external generalization. Among the two snpnet models from the same pan-trait UKB framework family (PGS000990 vs PGS001137) with essentially identical covariates and validation context, PGS001137 has the cleanest endpoint label (Retinal detachment) and stronger PRS-comparable metrics (higher PGS-only AUROC 0.573 vs 0.542; higher PGS-only R2 0.00663 vs 0.00213; higher incremental AUROC 0.0185 vs 0.0061). The two portability-study models (PGS001833, PGS002040) report only partial correlation (no PGS-only AUROC/R2), making them harder to compare directly despite slightly higher partial-r for PGS002040. Main limitation: evidence is confined to single-biobank framework/portability contexts with modest PRS-only performance and incomplete comparable metrics for two candidates, so the best choice is supported but not high-certainty.

Multiple direct-match rheumatoid arthritis PRS candidates are present (e.g., PGS001310, PGS002745, PGS002088, PGS004326, and the 2023 Am J Hum Genet five-biobank method-comparison family PGS003994–PGS004163). Among the endpoint-faithful options, PGS004163 is best supported by the visible evidence because it targets rheumatoid arthritis (trait_efo=rheumatoid arthritis) with a direct incident RA endpoint (phenotyping_reported="Seropositive RA"), uses an explicit multi-score aggregation method (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV), and shows the strongest reported discrimination within its coherent same-endpoint sibling cluster (full-model AUROC 0.7469 with OR 2.46 and R² 0.1376 in European validation). Main limitation: the reported AUROC/R² appear to be full-model metrics (covariates listed as "0" but no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R²), and the phenotype is seropositive RA rather than all RA, so while it is a strong direct match, comparability to a generic RA PRS remains somewhat uncertain from the provided metadata alone.

All four candidates are direct matches to sarcoidosis at the concept level, but the evidence is conflicted/limited. PGS000922 and PGS000923 are exact sarcoidosis EFO matches with explicit PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC (~0.64–0.65) and PGS-only R² (~0.017–0.018), and their R² values are below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.107), so the reported PRS signal is at least sanity-consistent. However, both come from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which the provided domain guidance flags as a systematic generalization weakness, and PGS000923 additionally uses a time-to-event endpoint (a noted warning signal for generic disease-risk use). The other two models (PGS001872, PGS002084) have a potential endpoint mismatch because trait_efo is ‘skin sarcoidosis’ despite ‘Sarcoidosis’ labels, and they lack PRS-comparable AUROC/R² (only partial correlation), making them harder to rank confidently. Between the two snpnet options, PGS000922 is preferred over the time-to-event variant due to cleaner endpoint alignment (non-TTE) with similar performance, but overall confidence remains low because all available options are framework-derived and/or have endpoint/metric limitations.

All five candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo = schizophrenia. However, endpoint fidelity differs: PGS000133/PGS000134/PGS000135/PGS000136 have phenotyping_reported = Schizophrenia (aligned), while PGS002785—despite schizophrenia labels—has phenotyping_reported = Cognitive function (Cognitive total), creating an explicit endpoint mismatch that weakens it as a schizophrenia PRS choice. Among the four endpoint-aligned siblings (same publication, method PRS-CS, similar covariates and EUR evaluation), the only visible differentiators are full-model AUROC and effect sizes; none reports PRS-only AUROC/R2, so full-model AUROC is discounted as a PRS-comparable metric. PGS000136 is preferred because it combines a higher full-model AUROC than two siblings (0.64 vs 0.60) with a strong reported per-SD OR (1.7), whereas PGS000135’s higher AUROC (0.74) lacks any effect size and is based on a much smaller validation sample (n=9,569), making its apparent advantage less well-supported in the visible evidence. Remaining limitation: the evidence is still sub-optimal because the key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2 or incremental metrics) are absent across the aligned sibling set, so the ranking relies on discounted full-model AUROC plus limited effect-size reporting.

All three candidates are direct matches with identical endpoint fields (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all indicate carcinoma in situ of skin) and similar basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4) in EUR-only training/evaluation, so phenotype alignment and comparability are strong across the set. None reports PRS-only AUROC/R2; only full-model AUROC and effect sizes are available, which limits confidence because full-model AUROC is not a PRS-comparable metric. Within this otherwise near-clone family, PGS000471 (lassosum, 7 variants) has the strongest visible validation signals: highest full-model AUROC (0.569 vs 0.557/0.524), highest Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0255 vs 0.0154/0.00141), and strongest per-SD OR (1.401 vs 1.308/1.09) and top-1% OR (3.77 vs 2.45/1.48). The main limitation is that these metrics are not explicitly PRS-only and the three models come from the same publication/cohort context, so the apparent performance differences may not translate to standalone PRS performance.

Direct-match candidates are present for sleep apnea, including generic “Sleep apnea” (PGS003204–PGS003218) and clinically dominant subtype “Obstructive sleep apnea” (PGS003479, PGS003857/PGS003858, PGS005219/PGS005220). Per domain knowledge, obstructive sleep apnea is the dominant clinical form of sleep apnea, so OSA-labeled models are acceptable direct matches when better supported. Among OSA models, PGS005220 is supported by (i) explicit OSA endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Obstructive sleep apnea), (ii) a disease-focused multi-cohort development context (FinnGen, MGBB, MVP), and (iii) stronger reported discrimination evidence than the ExPRSweb sleep-apnea framework cluster, which shows near-null full-model AUROCs (~0.49–0.53) and small effect sizes. Between the two 2025 OSA siblings, PGS005220 (UnadjustedBMI) is preferred over PGS005219 (AdjustedBMI) because BMI adjustment can attenuate the genetic signal relevant to generic sleep-apnea risk, while both otherwise share similar metadata and full-model AUROC reporting. Main limitation: the reported AUROC=0.79 is a full-model metric with covariates including BMI and no PGS-only AUROC/R2 is provided, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be isolated from the visible evidence, lowering confidence.

Multiple direct-match candidates exist with consistent endpoint alignment to squamous cell carcinoma (notably PGS000120 and the Cancer PRSweb SCC set PGS000460–PGS000468, plus PGS000731 and PGS005209). Among these, PGS000461 is best supported by the visible evidence because it has direct phenotype alignment (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported both squamous cell carcinoma), uses only basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), and shows the strongest reported effect-size evidence in this direct-match pool (OR per SD 1.491, 95% CI 1.395–1.593) alongside a relatively high full-model AUROC (0.599) and strong top-1% vs rest enrichment (OR 3.51). The main limitation is that the reported AUROC is a full-model metric (not explicitly PRS-only), and several near-clone SCC models (e.g., PGS000463/PGS000465) have very similar full-model AUROC and top-1% OR, making the winner not unequivocal; additionally, all evidence shown is EUR-only, limiting generalizability beyond European ancestry.

The direct-match search for the target trait "testicular carcinoma" returned zero models (total_found=0; models=[]), so there are no direct-match PRS candidates available in the provided context to evaluate or select among.

All listed candidates are direct matches to thyroid carcinoma via trait_efo=thyroid carcinoma and largely consistent trait_reported/phenotyping_reported (mostly “Thyroid cancer”). Among the strongest endpoint-faithful, non-restricted models, PGS000209 has a direct thyroid cancer endpoint, basic covariates (gender, birth year; no family history/treatment packaging), and large European evaluation (n=408,479) with reported AUROC 0.694 (95% CI 0.673–0.716). Competing candidates include PGS000208 with higher reported AUROC (0.751) but similarly covariate-adjusted full-model discrimination (not PRS-only) and PGS000797/PGS000087 from pan-cancer risk-factor integration contexts (less disease-focused), while PGS001354/PGS005210 are restricted to childhood cancer survivor “subsequent”/survivorship endpoints (endpoint mismatch for generic thyroid carcinoma). Because essentially all candidates lack clearly PRS-only (covariate-free) discrimination metrics and many AUROCs appear to be full-model values, the evidence is insufficient to declare a single unequivocal best model, so the selection remains sub-optimal despite a reasonable preference for the cleaner-covariate, large-evaluation PGS000209.

All listed candidates are direct matches at the trait_efo level (type 1 diabetes mellitus), but several have endpoint/covariate or study-archetype limitations. PGS000024 is best supported overall because its phenotyping_reported is a direct T1D diagnosis endpoint (good endpoint fidelity), it comes from a disease-focused T1D genetic risk score development/standardization study (Diabetes Care) rather than a pan-trait/portability framework, and it has strong reported discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.921) with very large validation support (n=374,000). Main limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric and covariates are listed as Unknown, so PRS-only performance comparability is unclear; competing models either have clearer PRS-only metrics but are from pan-trait/portability frameworks (e.g., PGS001297) or have potentially covariate-inflated full-model AUROC with explicit clinical covariates (e.g., PGS000021 includes islet auto-antibody status/BMI/age at diagnosis), reducing confidence that any single candidate is unequivocally best as a standalone PRS.

Direct-match candidates are abundant for type 2 diabetes mellitus. PGS000014 is a strong, disease-focused T2D PRS with clear phenotype alignment (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both Type 2 diabetes), a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) with very large variant count (6,917,436), multi-cohort training (DIAGRAM/EPIC/GERA/UKB), and explicit PRS-comparable signal reported (PGS-only Nagelkerke R2=0.029), which is below the provided liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.2191) and therefore passes the sanity check. However, several other direct-match candidates show higher full-model discrimination (e.g., PGS001781 full_model_auc=0.852; PGS000330 C-index=0.845), but these are not directly comparable PRS-only metrics and many candidates lack PRS-only AUC/R2, making it hard to identify a single clearly best model from the visible evidence alone; additionally, some high-AUC models use heavier clinical covariates (e.g., fasting glucose, lipids, family history), which discounts their apparent advantage. Therefore a direct match exists but the best-choice evidence is not decisive, yielding a sub-optimal direct-match recommendation with moderate confidence.

All 5 candidates are direct matches to ulcerative colitis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. Two candidates (PGS001306, PGS001307) come from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly despite having clean PGS-only metrics; additionally, PGS001307 is explicitly time-to-event, which is a mild endpoint penalty for a generic disease-risk target. Two candidates (PGS001855, PGS002066) come from a UKB portability framework paper (“Portability of 245 polygenic scores”) with limited PRS-comparable performance reporting here (partial-r only for PGS001855; low full-model AUROC=0.57 and OR CI crossing 1 for PGS002066, plus unknown covariates), making them weaker on comparable performance evidence. PGS004253 is disease-focused (UC PRS study context) with direct UC phenotyping, basic covariates, and strong reported effect size (OR per SD 1.84 with tight CI) plus full-model AUROC 0.66, making it the best-supported direct-match in this context. Limitation: PGS004253 does not report PGS-only AUROC/R² here (only full-model AUROC), and its training/validation sizes are smaller than the UKB framework models, so confidence is not high.

All 20 candidates are direct matches for urinary bladder cancer (trait_reported and/or trait_efo map to urinary bladder carcinoma/cancer; phenotyping_reported is bladder cancer/cancer of bladder/urothelial carcinoma). No model reports PRS-only AUROC/R2, so full-model AUROC values (including very high ~0.80 for PGS000071/PGS000782) are not comparable PRS metrics and are likely covariate-driven given inclusion of strong non-genetic predictors (age/sex/smoking/BMI), per the provided domain guidance. Among candidates with cleaner/basic covariates and comparable endpoints, the Cancer PRSweb ‘GWAS Hits’ family provides the strongest visible PRS signal: PGS000611 (13 variants; UKB development; age/sex/PCs covariates) shows a relatively higher full-model AUROC (0.567) and a notably stronger top-1% vs rest OR (2.66, 95% CI 1.79–3.93) than most other options shown, supporting better risk stratification. Main limitation: the key discriminative metrics are still full-model and not explicitly PRS-only, and several near-clone siblings (e.g., PGS000610/PGS000612/PGS000613) have very similar AUROC/OR-per-SD, so the preference for PGS000611 is not definitive.

All 5 candidates are direct matches to the target trait urolithiasis via either explicit urolithiasis/urinary calculus (PGS001864, PGS002075) or the closely synonymous ICD-style endpoint calculus of kidney and ureter / nephrolithiasis (PGS001250, PGS004493, PGS004563). Among models with PRS-comparable performance evidence, PGS002075 reports the strongest available PRS-only-like metric (partial correlation 0.0385, 95% CI 0.0246–0.0524) compared with PGS001864 (partial-r 0.0323), while the remaining newer nephrolithiasis models provide only modest per-SD ORs (~1.23–1.28) without AUC/R2 and with unknown covariates, limiting comparability. PGS001250 provides richer metric fields but comes from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper and its headline AUROC is largely full-model/covariate-driven, which domain guidance discounts versus cleaner PRS-comparable metrics. Overall, PGS002075 is the best-supported direct-match on the visible evidence, but confidence is limited because key discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2) are missing for most candidates and the partial-r metric is not directly comparable to AUROC/R2 across studies.

Direct-match candidates for the uterine cancer umbrella are present, including exact/near-exact uterine endpoints (PGS000541, PGS000542, PGS001795, PGS003740) and the clinically dominant subtype endometrial/uterine endometrial carcinoma (PGS000075, PGS000786, PGS002300, PGS002735-PGS002737, PGS003381, PGS004244). Domain knowledge states endometrial carcinoma is the dominant subtype of uterine carcinoma (~90%), so endometrial-carcinoma-labeled models are acceptable direct matches.

Among these, PGS003381 has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: uterine endometrial carcinoma), uses a genome-wide method (lassosum) with large variant count (529,365), and reports comparatively strong full-model discrimination (AUROC 0.761) with basic covariates (age, top 20 PCs), avoiding heavy clinical leakage. Competing exact-label uterine cancer models (PGS000541/PGS000542) have much lower AUROC (~0.57) and are sparse (18–20 variants). The framework-style uterine cancer model PGS001795 (PRS-CS-auto) has a direct label but shows very small PRS-comparable R2 (Nagelkerke’s R2 covariates-regressed-out 0.001948) and comes from a global biobank framework paper, which domain knowledge cautions often underperforms disease-focused alternatives.

Main limitation: PGS003381 does not provide explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 (only full-model AUROC/R2), so the PRS-only contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates; confidence is therefore Moderate rather than High.

All three candidates are direct concept matches to vitiligo by trait_reported/trait_efo, but they differ materially in endpoint fidelity. PGS000738 is the most endpoint-faithful: it comes from a vitiligo-focused publication and reports the trait as Vitiligo, whereas PGS000760’s phenotyping_reported is explicitly treatment/context-specific (anti-PD-L1 induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients), making its vitiligo label less directly aligned to generic vitiligo risk. PGS001536 is a pan-trait UK Biobank framework score ("across 813 traits") with a time-to-event endpoint, which domain guidance flags as less reliable than disease-focused models despite having explicit AUROC/R2. Performance evidence is limited/incomplete for the disease-focused option (PGS000738 lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2 and has unknown covariates; only a pseudo R² is shown), so while PGS000738 is preferred on phenotype alignment and study focus, the overall recommendation remains sub-optimal due to missing comparable PRS-only metrics and some metadata ambiguity.
